spec.title: A Door Left Ajar
spec.intent: A 180-second late-night noir jazz meditation in which tenor saxophone and piano exchange evolving phrases across contrasting upper-harmony phases, with the unresolved pedal reserved for the opening and coda.

tempo.feel: Sparse, slow behind-the-beat swing in 4/4, with brushes entering only at phrase turns.

tonality.mode: Modal minor with shifting upper harmony and pedal-point ambiguity

instrumentation.name: tenor saxophone
instrumentation.role: Foreground melodic voice using spacious call-and-response phrases with piano, gradually ornamenting and fragmenting its material.
instrumentation.timbre: Warm, breathy, restrained, softly vibrated, never forceful.

instrumentation.name: piano
instrumentation.role: Introduces contrasting upper-harmony phases and answers the saxophone with spacious voicings and short motifs.
instrumentation.timbre: Muted, intimate, softly resonant, colored by suspended tones, upper triads, and restrained blues inflections.

instrumentation.name: upright bass
instrumentation.role: Establishes a calm two-note pedal in the opening, then supports the evolving harmony before returning to the pedal in the coda.
instrumentation.timbre: Deep, woody, rounded, gently pizzicato with occasional sustained resonance.

instrumentation.name: brush kit
instrumentation.role: Marks phrase turns and lightly supports the slow swing without a strong backbeat.
instrumentation.timbre: Dry, featherlight brush swirls with minimal cymbal brightness.

structure.direction: Upright bass establishes the two-note pedal alone; piano adds isolated voicings. Keep the room quiet and spacious.
Tenor saxophone enters with a long-breathed phrase. Piano answers rather than merely accompanying; brushes appear only at phrase turns.

Release the fixed pedal and let piano move through contrasting upper-harmony phases: suspended dominants, modal minor colors, upper triads, and restrained blues inflections. Saxophone responds in call-and-response, with gentle ornamentation and no flashy soloing.
Shorten the exchanges, increase silence, and thin the brushes. Let saxophone fragments and piano replies pass through softer, more ambiguous harmonic colors.
Return the upright bass to the two-note pedal. Reduce the dialogue to a final saxophone breath, sparse piano voicing, and softly unresolved decay.

spec.production: Intimate tactile acoustic quartet recording in a dark, warm room. Keep the tenor saxophone forward but gentle, piano clearly articulate yet spacious, bass rounded and low, and brushes subdued. Use natural reverb, restrained dynamics, soft transient detail, and a quiet stereo image with no dramatic climax.
assumptions: Set the tempo near 58 BPM for the specified slow swing.
Use shifting modal upper harmony without imposing a fixed tonic.
Reserve the two-note pedal strictly for the opening and coda.
spec.lyriaPrompt: Late-night noir jazz meditation for relaxation, approximately 180 seconds, instrumental only, no vocals. Slow 4/4 swing around 58 BPM, sparse and slightly behind the beat, with tactile acoustic playing, restrained dynamics, spacious phrasing, and a dark warm room. [Intro] Begin with deep upright bass repeating a calm two-note pedal while intimate piano adds isolated suspended voicings. [Theme] Bring in a warm, breathy tenor saxophone; have saxophone and piano exchange long, spacious call-and-response phrases, with featherlight brushes entering only at phrase turns. [Harmonic Dialogue] Release the pedal and let piano introduce contrasting upper-harmony phases—modal minor colors, suspended dominants, upper triads, and restrained blues inflections—while the tenor saxophone responds with subtle ornamentation, never a flashy solo. [Fragmentation] Shorten the exchanges, increase silence, and thin the brushes as saxophone phrases break into gentle echoes. [Coda] Return the upright bass to the two-note pedal, reduce to a sparse piano voicing and fading tenor breath, and end softly unresolved. Avoid vocals, strong backbeat, bright cymbals, abrupt drops, cinematic bombast, and definitive cadence.
